summary: This Mol Labs public report (P15) proposes a hypothesis-testing assay to determine whether residual BPC-157-driven HUVEC tube formation and migration under VEGFR2 blockade (which abolishes VEGF-A tubes) requires FBXO22 (via siFBXO22 loss-of-function). The document frames this as a "stabilizer-vs-receptor" assumption-kill experiment, explicitly distinct from a prior orthosteric-binding/SPR-vs-ECD-only study (OpenLabs 8e5ba06c). The experiment has NOT been run; the key result (residual BPC-157 tubes/migration abolished by siFBXO22 under VEGFR2 block) is a pre-registered prediction, with all supporting data currently from literature.

content_blocks.title: Claim / Hypothesis
content_blocks.content: On a matched HUVEC tube-formation/migration panel where VEGFR2 blockade (TKI/block) abolishes VEGF-A tubes, residual BPC-157 tubes/migration are abolished by FBXO22 LOF (siFBXO22) on the same panel. This is framed as an 'assumption-kill / stabilizer-vs-receptor' test. Explicitly NOT the orthosteric-binding/SPR-vs-ECD-only dialect of OpenLabs 8e5ba06c-5f1e-4970-b740-9955c137cad3.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: Hsieh-class HUVEC tubes activate a VEGFR2–Akt–eNOS axis (dynasore blocks internalization/tubes — endocytosis, not a VEGFR2 TKI residual panel). Zhang places physical engagement on intracellular FBXO22–BACH1 (SPR KD from literature; FBXO22 KD abolishes BPC→BACH1 protein rise; BACH1 KD reverses BPC tubes). Physical VEGFR2 binding remains unclear per Zhang. P15 scores residual BPC-157 tubes/migration under a VEGFR2 TKI/block that first abolishes VEGF-A tubes, then asks whether that residual still requires FBXO22 (siFBXO22) on the same HUVEC panel.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art Summary
content_blocks.content:
Four key literature references are cited:
1. PMID 27847966 (Hsieh 2017): BPC-157 CAM/HUVEC tubes; VEGFR2 mRNA/protein upregulation (VEGF-A not upregulated); internalization; VEGFR2–Akt–eNOS axis; dynasore blocks internalization/pathway/tubes. No VEGFR2 ECD KD; dynasore ≠ VEGFR2 TKI residual × FBXO22 H2H.
2. PMID 41606641 (Zhang 2026, DOI 10.1186/s12964-026-02694-6, PMC12947506): BPC-157–FBXO22 SPR KD = 1.0×10⁻⁷ M (100 nM); scramble KD = 2.6×10⁻⁴ M; FBXO22 KD abolishes BPC→BACH1 protein rise; BACH1 KD reverses BPC HUVEC tubes; physical VEGFR2 binding unresolved. No VEGFR2-block residual panel.
3. PMID 33051481 (Huang/Hsieh 2020): Src–Cav-1–eNOS/vasomotor follow-up of VEGFR2-axis work. No VEGFR2 ECD binding assay; no VEGFR2 TKI residual × FBXO22 panel.
4. PMID 31911270 (2020): Bach1 suppresses angiogenesis (BTB-dependent) in ischemic/endothelial models — anti-angiogenic sign-conflict adjacent to Zhang BACH1-as-effector; not residual-under-VEGFR2-block H2H.

content_blocks.title: Baseline Claimed vs. Baseline Measured
content_blocks.content:
Claimed baseline: Under VEGFR2 blockade that abolishes VEGF-A HUVEC tube formation, BPC-157 still drives tubes/migration that FBXO22 LOF abolishes on the same panel.
Measured baseline: All supporting data is from literature only. Matched residual-BPC under VEGFR2 block abolishing VEGF-A × FBXO22 LOF on same HUVEC panel is UNKNOWN (soft-complete BPC∩VEGFR2∩FBXO22∩(block|TKI|LOF) = 0 PubMed hits; VEGFR2-TKI∩BPC = 0; orthosteric-SPR∩BPC∩VEGFR2 = 0). Residual BPC under VEGFR2 block abolished by siFBXO22 is a PREDICTION only.

content_blocks.title: Proposed Method / Assay Design
content_blocks.content: Method type: propose-assay. Execution status: NOT_RUN. Design: Matched HUVEC tube-formation/migration panel. Step 1: VEGFR2 TKI/block abolishes VEGF-A tubes (QC gate). Step 2: Score residual BPC-157 tubes/migration under that block. Step 3: Apply siFBXO22 (optional siBACH1) and score FBXO22 dependence of residual BPC-157 phenotype. Optional secondary: VEGFR2 ECD SPR. Require VEGF-A abolish under block, then score residual BPC and FBXO22 dependence. α/N pre-specified. Do not invent observed %/KD/dosing.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. Do not treat P1–P14 as proving P15 — P1 unbridged Hsieh vs Zhang / ECD KD emptiness is not a residual-under-VEGFR2-block × FBXO22 LOF panel; soft-complete empty ≠ demonstrated residual phenotype.
2. Skip-list distinctness (critical) — do not freeze or collapse to OpenLabs 8e5ba06c ('BPC-157 is not orthosteric VEGFR2' / SPR-vs-ECD-only) or 7db12286; optional SPR secondary only; REJECT if claim drifts to orthosteric-only.
3. Hsieh dynasore ≠ VEGFR2 TKI residual panel; Zhang FBXO22/BACH1 axis has no VEGFR2-block arm; Bach1 sign conflict adjacent ≠ H2H; incomplete VEGF-A abolish / incomplete FBXO22 KD leave the test inconclusive rather than refuted; no dosing; NOT FOXO4×LOF.

content_blocks.title: Refutation Criteria
content_blocks.content: Refute if: On the pre-registered matched HUVEC tube/migration panel where VEGFR2 TKI/block abolishes VEGF-A tubes, residual BPC-157 tubes/migration are NOT abolished by FBXO22 LOF (siFBXO22) relative to control-genotype residual under the same block — so receptor-block-alone / FBXO22-independent residual framing survives and stabilizer-vs-receptor residual-dependence fails — when incomplete VEGF-A abolish gate, absent residual under block, incomplete FBXO22 knockdown, or dynasore-misread artifacts are ruled out.

content_blocks.title: Key Quantitative Data from Literature
content_blocks.content: From Zhang 2026 (PMID 41606641): BPC-157–FBXO22 SPR KD = 1.0×10⁻⁷ M (100 nM); scramble control KD = 2.6×10⁻⁴ M. FBXO22 KD abolishes BPC→BACH1 protein rise. BACH1 KD reverses BPC HUVEC tubes. Physical VEGFR2 binding remains unresolved. From Hsieh 2017 (PMID 27847966): VEGFR2 mRNA/protein upregulated by BPC-157; VEGF-A not upregulated; dynasore blocks internalization/pathway/tubes.

key_findings: Experiment NOT RUN — P15 is a pre-registered prediction/proposed assay, not a completed experiment; execution_status=NOT_RUN.
Core hypothesis: Residual BPC-157 HUVEC tube formation/migration under VEGFR2 TKI/block (which abolishes VEGF-A tubes) is abolished by FBXO22 LOF (siFBXO22) — stabilizer-vs-receptor assumption-kill.
All quantitative data is from literature: BPC-157–FBXO22 SPR KD = 100 nM (Zhang 2026, PMID 41606641); scramble KD = 2.6×10⁻⁴ M.
Zhang 2026 (PMID 41606641): FBXO22 KD abolishes BPC→BACH1 protein rise; BACH1 KD reverses BPC HUVEC tubes; no VEGFR2-block residual arm.
Hsieh 2017 (PMID 27847966): BPC-157 activates VEGFR2–Akt–eNOS axis in HUVEC/CAM; dynasore blocks internalization/tubes — but dynasore ≠ VEGFR2 TKI residual panel.
Soft-complete literature search: BPC∩VEGFR2∩FBXO22∩(block|TKI|LOF) = 0 PubMed hits; VEGFR2-TKI∩BPC = 0 — matched residual H2H panel is UNKNOWN.
FTO status: UNKNOWN; IP class: stabilizer-vs-receptor; kill_cost_tier=1; estimated time_to_refute=4 weeks.
Explicitly distinct from OpenLabs 8e5ba06c (orthosteric VEGFR2 / SPR-vs-ECD-only); P1–P14 do not prove P15.
Bach1 anti-angiogenic prior (PMID 31911270) creates sign-conflict adjacent to Zhang BACH1-as-effector framing — not resolved by existing literature.
Model system proposed: HUVEC tube-formation/migration assay with VEGFR2 TKI/block, siFBXO22 (optional siBACH1), BPC-157 vs VEGF-A comparators, optional secondary VEGFR2 ECD SPR.
